sources.title: OpenAI, Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch (2026-09-24 preprint)
sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 and its complete proof, Sections 2–8, PDF pp. 2–40 (43-page full paper). The full proof was fetched and read; its novel continuation estimates and global extension have not been independently validated here.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1, smooth anisotropic uniqueness from one patch
contents.reason: This preprint claims the exact open conclusion, but its lengthy proof has not been independently checked; owner review must decide whether it closes the open-problem status.

contents.name: Corollary 1.2, full-boundary uniqueness
contents.reason: This full-boundary consequence depends on Theorem 1.1, whose proof is pending independent owner review.

contents.name: Corollary 1.3, smooth scalar conductivity uniqueness
contents.reason: The assigned pair concerns anisotropic gauge and geometric uniqueness, not the separate Euclidean scalar-conductivity consequence in Section 8.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1, equality of boundary metric jets
contents.reason: The boundary-symbol recursion supports the claimed new proof and is not treated as established until its derivation is independently reviewed.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2, common exterior cap and Green data
contents.reason: The minimization comparison and Green-kernel transfer are part of the unverified proof chain, so this proposition is not imported.

contents.name: Lemma 2.3, source-generated separation and harmonic jets
contents.reason: The point-supported distribution and unique-continuation argument is read but has not been independently checked for all stated jet claims.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1, local metric extension across a hypersurface
contents.reason: This is the central smooth-coefficient continuation theorem; its proof relies on the later weighted estimates and remains under owner review.

contents.name: Lemma 3.2, product extension from a cross
contents.reason: The singular-function series and interpolation-exponent argument is not used as a supplier pending independent verification.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3, product extension criterion from Hessian convex separation
contents.reason: The convex-separation reduction and strict-weight construction require a separate complete check before the claimed theorem can be accepted.

contents.name: Lemma 3.4, propagation through a compact cylinder
contents.reason: The finite-cover gluing and overlap agreement support the unverified continuation argument and are not imported.

contents.name: Proposition 3.5, fixed-separation initialization of the mixed Green kernel
contents.reason: The two-stage continuation and uniform positive-separation bounds have not been independently validated.

contents.name: Lemma 4.1, profile and shrinking-radius estimates
contents.reason: These parameter-uniform profile estimates feed the main contraction argument and remain subject to owner review.

contents.name: Proposition 4.2, continuation to the moving sphere family
contents.reason: The strict Hessian calculation at moving spheres is a crucial new estimate and is not certified by reading the preprint alone.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3, representing density for the transfer functional
contents.reason: The moving-sphere representation and uniform cutoff-region bounds form part of the unverified argument.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1, differentiated moving trace equation
contents.reason: The parameter-dependent boundary operator expansion and its remainder classes require independent scrutiny.

contents.name: Lemma 5.2, weighted spherical-harmonic raising estimate
contents.reason: The degree-by-degree coercivity calculation is technically substantial and has not been certified here.

contents.name: Proposition 5.3, coercivity for the moving trace equation
contents.reason: The principal perturbation commutators and derivative-count bounds are central to the proof and remain unverified.

contents.name: Lemma 5.4, uniform transfer-density bound
contents.reason: This estimate depends on the preceding coercivity proposition, so no bound is accepted before that argument is checked.

contents.name: Lemma 6.1, two-power moment bound
contents.reason: The cancellation of affine moments is stated and read, but its dependence on the unverified transfer bound remains open.

contents.name: Lemma 6.2, finite-order interpolation
contents.reason: Although this interpolation step is elementary, it is only used inside the not-yet-validated proof chain.

contents.name: Lemma 6.3, superlinear improvement of the metric bound
contents.reason: This improvement closes the contraction argument and must be checked together with its uniform-radius hypotheses.

contents.name: Proposition 7.1, absence of an interior frontier
contents.reason: The global maximal-isometry extension depends on the unverified local metric extension theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 7.2, smooth completion and accessible gauge
contents.reason: The boundary completion and recovery of the exact measured-patch gauge are not accepted until the global proof is independently reviewed.

contents.name: Lemma 8.1, conformal rigidity at a boundary patch
contents.reason: The lemma supports the paper's separate scalar-conductivity corollary, which is outside this anisotropic gauge and uniqueness pair.
